Why this exists: checkAnswer.js compares answerType 'string' literally --
parsed = attempt, then _equality. But _equality takes an array, so the
platform already accepts a list of correct answers. Only the tooling
discards it: create_content.py:265 hardcodes stepAnswer: [answer]. So we
Without this every Data 100 problem is effectively unsolvable: the regex
answers are stored with literal surrounding backticks, which no
Scope: _equality now normalises whitespace, quote style and the
backtick / r"" wrappers on both sides, so those no longer need listing.
List only patterns that are genuinely, semantically correct.
A key is normally a problem name. Use the full content-pool directory
name when one problem appears in both lessons of a course and each copy
keeps a different step -- their correct answers differ.

row5.note: Data_yesChat P1. Course IDs of exactly three digits.

row4.note: Data_noChat P3. Capture the street name following the street number in '123 San Pablo Ave, 94702'.

note: Data_yesChat P2, S25FQ1B step (i): keep only the rooms whose
'renovated' is recorded. Keyed by directory because Data_noChat P4 is
the same problem on a different step.
NOT accepted, and deliberately: rooms.dropna() (drops any row with any
NA, not just renovated) and rooms[rooms['renovated'] != None] (does not
work in pandas) are the source's own distractors.
Data_noChat P4, S25FQ1B step (ii): a building is modern when at least
80% of its rooms with recorded renovations were renovated in 2003 or
later. Long free-entry answer -- expect a low correct rate; noChat sets
giveStuFeedback: false, so a wrong answer still advances.
NOT accepted: (...>= 2003).sum() >= 0.80, a source distractor that
compares a count against a proportion.
